title: CF Meet enterprise calling bodies v1
description: Request and response bodies of Calling's enterprise calling API (Part F sections 52-62): the typed enterprise call policy, departments, extensions, ring groups, call queues, IVR flows, business hours, forwarding rules, voicemail mailboxes and messages, call-recording policies and recordings, administrative audit and the enterprise call context. Scope (tenant, application, environment) comes only from the authenticated credential and is never a body field. Mutations of existing resources carry expectedVersion. No body carries a raw telephone number (public forwarding targets are opaque ContactReferences), a provider, SIP or edge identifier, a DTMF digit sequence, an object-storage key or a public media URL. The root accepts exactly one of the bodies (fixtures); the HTTP contract references the $defs.

Never a URL, path, file name or synthesized text. Each prompt has a nominal length the media plane's audio must fit (WELCOME, MENU, NO_INPUT, GOODBYE 2 s; PLEASE_HOLD, TRANSFERRING, CLOSED 3 s; INVALID_OPTION 4 s; VOICEMAIL_GREETING 6 s; BEEP 1 s): a menu's input timer starts after the prompts it queued, and a HANGUP node's prompt plays for its nominal length before the platform ends the Call.

VoicemailMessageState.description: RECORDING: the edge / capture adapter is capturing. PROCESSING: the audio arrived and is being stored (a storage outage keeps it here while the deliverer retries — never a fake READY). READY: stored in protected object storage. FAILED: the capture failed or never arrived (a late delivery can still make it READY). DELETING: deletion requested (user, administrator or retention); the object is being removed. DELETED: the object is gone; the row and the originating Call's history remain.

There is no 'everyone consented' flag. Replaying the same decision is idempotent; a DECLINED by a participant a running recording relies on stops it (CONSENT_WITHDRAWN).

DELETING / DELETED: removed (user, administrator or retention); the Call's history remains.

RecordingAuthorization.description: An immutable, server-authoritative recording decision taken before any capture.

oneOf.description: Opaque reference to the compliance configuration this policy implements (e.g. NG-NDPA-2023/v2). Authoritative input from compliance / legal — the platform never infers recording law from a country. Never a telephone number.

RecordingAuthorizationList.description: The recording decisions of a Call (oldest first).

RecordingMediaAccess.description: A short-lived (at most 300 s), read-only, single-object signed URL minted AFTER authorization and audited; never stored.
